capabilities: Mask completed words as Unicode glyphs while typing
Reveal text on selection, hover, or cursor placement
Automatically mask sensitive patterns like emails, API keys, and credit cards
Exclude individual notes and folders from masking via frontmatter and paths
Auto-mask after idle time or when the Obsidian window loses focus
disambiguation: Not an encryption or security tool; it only changes how characters look on screen and does not protect files on disk.
extras: README explicitly warns the plugin is only a visual shoulder-surfing deterrent, not encryption; MIT licensed and part of the YABP initiative; also installable manually or via BRAT.
problem: Obsidian shows note text in plain form, so anyone nearby in an office, cafe, or classroom can read your screen while you write.

relations.evidence: Open BRAT settings and select Add Beta plugin.

summary: Visual privacy layer that masks completed words as Matrix-style glyphs on screen while leaving the underlying note files untouched.
